# name: single_example_parity_contrast
# description: Among one-example sets, yes-rate for targets sharing the example's parity minus yes-rate for opposite-parity targets; observed above null means the model under-produces parity generalisation from a single example.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    n = s.str.count(",") + 1
    m = n == 1
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    ex = pd.to_numeric(s[m], errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values[m.values]
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values[m.values]
    same = (ex % 2) == (t % 2)
    a = r[same].mean() if same.any() else 0.0
    b = r[~same].mean() if (~same).any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/single_example_distance_slope.py
# name: single_example_distance_slope
# description: Among one-example sets, OLS slope of yes (0/1) on |target - example|/100; a more negative observed value than null means people generalise more by numeric proximity from one example than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    m = (s.str.count(",") == 0).values
    if m.sum() < 3:
        return 0.0
    ex = pd.to_numeric(s[m], errors="coerce").fillna(0).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values[m]
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values[m]
    x = np.abs(t - ex) / 100.0
    v = x.var()
    if v <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((x - x.mean()) * (r - r.mean())).mean() / v)
EOF

# name: far_target_yes_size_slope
# description: Slope of the yes-rate for targets lying >15 outside the example range against set size (1-4); observed less negative than null means the model shrinks far-target generalisation with more examples too strongly.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    lo = sp.min(axis=1).values
    hi = sp.max(axis=1).values
    n = sp.notna().sum(axis=1).values.astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    far = (t < lo - 15) | (t > hi + 15)
    xs, ys = [], []
    for k in (1, 2, 3, 4):
        mk = far & (n == k)
        if mk.sum() > 0:
            xs.append(k); ys.append(r[mk].mean())
    if len(xs) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.polyfit(np.array(xs, float), np.array(ys), 1)[0])
EOF

# name: mid_span_interior_yes
# description: Among sets of 2+ examples, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the example range; observed above null means the model under-produces interval (range-filling) generalisation.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    lo = sp.min(axis=1).values
    hi = sp.max(axis=1).values
    n = sp.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    isex = (sp.values == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & (~isex)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).values[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/outlier_rule_far_yes.py
# name: outlier_rule_far_yes
# description: For 3-4 example sets where all but exactly one example share a last digit, yes-rate for out-of-range targets with that shared last digit; observed above null means the model is too intolerant of the exception (under-keeps the near-fitting rule), below means too tolerant.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    v = sp.values
    n = np.isfinite(v).sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(v, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(v, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ld = np.where(np.isfinite(v), np.mod(np.nan_to_num(v), 10), -1)
    best_cnt = np.zeros(len(t)); best_d = np.full(len(t), -1.0)
    for d in range(10):
        c = (ld == d).sum(axis=1)
        upd = c > best_cnt
        best_cnt = np.where(upd, c, best_cnt); best_d = np.where(upd, d, best_d)
    m = (n >= 3) & (best_cnt == n - 1) & (np.mod(t, 10) == best_d) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[m].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/single_example_multiple_contrast.py
# name: single_example_multiple_contrast
# description: Among one-example sets with example >= 3, yes-rate for targets that are multiples or divisors (>1) of the example minus other targets; observed above null means the model under-produces multiplicative generalisation from one example.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    m = (s.str.count(",") == 0).values
    ex = pd.to_numeric(s[m], errors="coerce").fillna(1).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values[m]
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values[m]
    keep = ex >= 3
    ex, t, r = ex[keep], t[keep], r[keep]
    if len(t) == 0:
        return 0.0
    rel = ((t % ex) == 0) | (((ex % np.maximum(t, 1)) == 0) & (t > 1))
    a = r[rel].mean() if rel.any() else 0.0
    b = r[~rel].mean() if (~rel).any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/decade_boundary_contrast.py
# name: decade_boundary_contrast
# description: For 2+ example sets all in one decade, yes-rate for non-example targets in that decade minus targets within 5 outside it; observed above null means the model under-weights decade boundaries (people respect decades more sharply).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    v = sp.values
    n = np.isfinite(v).sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(v, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(v, axis=1)
    dlo = np.floor((lo - 1) / 10); dhi = np.floor((hi - 1) / 10)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dt = np.floor((t - 1) / 10)
    isex = (v == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & (dlo == dhi) & (~isex)
    inside = base & (dt == dlo)
    a0 = dlo * 10 + 1; a1 = dlo * 10 + 10
    near = base & (dt != dlo) & (((t < a0) & (t >= a0 - 5)) | ((t > a1) & (t <= a1 + 5)))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or near.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[near].mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/late_minus_early_yes.py
# name: late_minus_early_yes
# description: Yes-rate on trials in the top third of trial_index minus the bottom third; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means the static model misses a drift in willingness to say yes over the session.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    q1, q2 = np.quantile(ti, [1/3, 2/3])
    a = r[ti >= q2]; b = r[ti <= q1]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())
EOF
cat << 'EOF' > $D/set_yes_rate_spread.py
# name: set_yes_rate_spread
# description: Standard deviation across sets of each set's overall yes-rate (non-example targets); observed above null means the model makes sets too similar in breadth (under-differentiates rule-like vs diffuse sets).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    isex = (sp.values == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    sub = df.loc[~isex]
    g = sub.groupby(sub["number_set"].astype(str))["rating"].mean()
    if len(g) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(g.std())
EOF

I wrote the 8 test statistics to `iter_4/critique/test_stats/`. None of them imports anything, which is what knocked out every statistic on the first attempt; they use only the `np`, `pd` and `math` already in scope. I ran each one once on the observed data: all return a finite float in under 0.03 s and are vectorised. I did not run the posterior-predictive harness, so there are no p-values yet.

| Statistic | What it probes | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `single_example_parity_contrast` | One-example sets: "yes" rate for same-parity targets minus opposite-parity targets (odd/even generalisation from one number) | 0.326 |
| `single_example_multiple_contrast` | One-example sets (example ≥ 3): "yes" rate for multiples or divisors of the example minus other targets | 0.245 |

def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)

    v = sp.values
    n = np.isfinite(v).sum(axis=1)

    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    ld = np.where(np.isfinite(v), np.mod(np.nan_to_num(v), 10), -1)
    best_cnt = np.zeros(len(t)); best_d = np.full(len(t), -1.0)
    for d in range(10):
        c = (ld == d).sum(axis=1)

    m = (n >= 3) & (best_cnt == n - 1) & (np.mod(t, 10) == best_d) & ((t < lo) | (t > hi))

# name: decade_boundary_contrast
# description: For 2+ example sets all in one decade, yes-rate for non-example targets in that decade minus targets within 5 outside it; observed above null means the model under-weights decade boundaries (people respect decades more sharply).
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    sp = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    v = sp.values
    n = np.isfinite(v).sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(v, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(v, axis=1)
    dlo = np.floor((lo - 1) / 10); dhi = np.floor((hi - 1) / 10)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    dt = np.floor((t - 1) / 10)
    isex = (v == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & (dlo == dhi) & (~isex)
    inside = base & (dt == dlo)
    a0 = dlo * 10 + 1; a1 = dlo * 10 + 10
    near = base & (dt != dlo) & (((t < a0) & (t >= a0 - 5)) | ((t > a1) & (t <= a1 + 5)))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or near.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[near].mean())

# description: Yes-rate on trials in the top third of trial_index minus the bottom third; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means the static model misses a drift in willingness to say yes over the session.
